answer: Max-flow trust networks resist Sybil attacks by granting agent privileges only when a key receives sufficient min-cut flow from verified anchors. Transient comet identities remain isolated across a sparse graph canyon because honest peers cap outgoing edge weights. To extract protocol nectar like unsecured credit, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring distinct incoming capacity per identity. However, compromising high-centrality hubs widens that cut for fake clones.
